name: Greyish umber

sections.title: Greyish umber is a dark, neutral grey-brown carried into our library from the Japanese traditional color Ainezumi, "mousy indigo," and it sits in a crowded ISCC-NBS neighborhood that also holds names like Argali, Goat and Mordore.
sections.body:
The nearest named colors on file are [[bone-brown]], [[grebe]], [[zinc-grey]] and [[starling]], at 2.8, 2.9, 2.9 and 3.4 ΔE [1]. No book consulted independently dates the coinage beyond that library gloss, so it is undocumented here [1].

The swatch measures lightness 36, chroma 5 and hue 66 degrees, filed under Neutrals and used chiefly for painter's pigments, 4.9 units from [[umber]] [1]. The ISCC-NBS 1955 block that covers this neighborhood (block 64) carries two dozen other alternate names for nearby shades, including Goat and Mordore, both dated by Maerz and Paul to 1930 as first recorded in 1705 and 1791 respectively, and Argali, first recorded 1925 [1]. A greener cousin at the same depth is [[greenish-umber]] [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: A color within range of this swatch appears in 2,775 of the 23,781 paintings in our archive, about 11.7 percent, as photographed, chiefly in mid-tones [2]. Vilhelm Hammershøi carries it in 26 of 50 dated paintings, 4.5 times the archive's overall rate[2]. A date of 17 recorded for one early match, Jacques Linard's *Still Life with Plums*, is a known gap in the archive's date field and is not used here as a reliable year [2].
